messages.subject: lavPredict(): Error in solve.default()
parts:
Hi,

I have fitted a series of longitudinal models, all with three occasions, and one factor per occasion each loading on three binary indicators. For a model that simply correlates the three factors and for a second-order growth curve model, lavPredict() works as expected. But for a latent change score model, I get the following error:

Error in solve.default(VETAx[[g]]) :
  system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number = 2.11011e-18

The model was estimated using the lavaan() function using DWLS (theta parameterization) with listwise deletion. I'll paste the model definition and the summary output below. Any help with determining what's going wrong would be appreciated. Thanks!

nfcc_g1 =~ l_qnfc2 * qnfc2g1 + l_qnfc12 * qnfc12g1 + l_qnfc14 * qnfc14g1
nfcc_g3 =~ l_qnfc2 * qnfc2g3 + l_qnfc12 * qnfc12g3 + l_qnfc14 * qnfc14g3
nfcc_g5 =~ l_qnfc2 * qnfc2g5 + l_qnfc12 * qnfc12g5 + l_qnfc14 * qnfc14g5

# Effects coding constraint for loadings

# Latent variable (residual) variances
nfcc_g1 ~~ nfcc_g1

# Latent variable intercepts
nfcc_g1 ~ 1
nfcc_g3 ~ 0

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: lavPredict(): Error in solve.default()
parts:
Ulrich,
  If I understand correctly, the error was produced by lavPredict() not by the original lavaan() fit.  My guess is that the error reflects the fact that the difference variables are a determinate function of the common factor variables.

  According to the lavPredict() documentation file, the structural model has no impact on the factor score estimates.  So, why not just accept the common-factor factor-score estimates for the model without the latent differences?  Then compute the differences between the common-factor factor-score estimates.

myEstimates <- lavPredict(fit)
d_nfcc_g3_estimate <- myEstimates[,2] - myEstimates[,1]
d_nfcc_g5_estimate <- myEstimates[,3] - myEstimates[,2]
myEstimates <- cbind(myEstimates, d_nfcc_g3_estimate, d_nfcc_g5_estimate)

Keith

messages.subject: Re: lavPredict(): Error in solve.default()
parts:
Thanks Keith. I’d come across the part of the documentation that talks about the structural part of the model being ignored for prediction. I assumed that this must mean something else because lavPredict() happily gave me factor scores for all latent variables in a second-order growth curve model, including the (second-order) intercept and slope factors, which to my understanding do in fact belong to the structural part of the model.

What the documentation says is:

"NOTE: the goal of this function is NOT to predict future values of dependent variables as in the regression framework!”

And further below:

"Note that this function can not be used to ‘predict’ values of dependent variables, given the values of independent values (in the regression sense). In other words, the structural component is completely ignored (for now).”

To me that seemed to indicate not that there is a limitation that excludes dependent variables or the structural model from factor score estimation, but that the purpose of lavaan’s predict() and lavPredict() functions is different from the generic predict() function used in the regression framework. The former computes factor scores, while the latter predicts values of the dependent variables given values of the explanatory variables.

Thanks also for the hint regarding computing the difference scores from the correlation model. That would work of course, except that I would not get standard errors for the differences.

Uli

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: lavPredict(): Error in solve.default()
parts:
Ulrich,
  I can give you my exegesis of the help file but will defer to someone else to answer your question about standard errors.

  Every so often, someone asks a question based on the expectation that lavPredict() should work like the generic predict() in R.  They expect predicted values of the dependent (endogenous in the syntactical sense) variables, predicted from supplied values of the independent (exogenous) variables.  I believe that both the passages that you quoted are intended to ward users off that mistaken expectation.  The passages do not mean that factor scores will not be estimated for variables that are endogenous.  They mean that factor scores are estimated, not predicted scores, for all latent variables, regardless of whether they are endogenous or exogenous.  Essentially, the model is treated like a CFA model.

  Higher order factors have their own residuals/disturbances.  So, unlike latent differences, they are not co-linear with other latent variables in the model.  To illustrate the colinearity issue, I reproduced the same error by fitting the lavPredict example modified to fix the correlation between the first two factors to 1.

# fit model
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9
              visual ~~ 1*textual
              visual ~~ 1*visual
              textual ~~ 1*textual
              speed ~~ 1*speed
' # end model
    
fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, auto.fix.first=FALSE)
head(lavPredict(fit)) # error
head(lavPredict(fit, type = "ov")) # okay (nothing to estimate, no matrix to invert)
